about: The graphics driver settings Rig reads and changes, shared by the server, the app (packages/core/src/gpu.ts) and the helper (helper/RigHelper/Gpu.cs, embedded). Only NVIDIA's for now, through its driver settings database (DRS). Ids and values are NVIDIA's own, from NvApiDriverSettings.h in github.com/NVIDIA/nvapi (MIT). A setting's `values` say what each choice sets: one or more DRS ids, each to one value. A choice is read back when every id it sets holds its value. `range` takes a whole number for one id instead of a named choice. `defaults` are the driver's own values, used when an id is set nowhere. `scope: global` means the setting is for the whole PC, never one game. `tier` is the card's risk: every one here is put back exactly by Rig's undo. `windowsApps` are Windows' own programs, which a change is never made for (a read of them is fine).

lowLatency.name: Low latency mode
lowLatency.says: How many frames the CPU may line up ahead of the graphics card. On cuts input lag in games the graphics card holds back.

on.says: On: at most one frame waits

maxFrameRate.name: Max frame rate
maxFrameRate.says: A cap on frames a second, set in the driver.

vsync.name: Vertical sync
vsync.says: Whether frames wait for the screen's refresh. Off tears but has the least lag; Fast is for frame rates well above the refresh rate.

adaptive.says: Adaptive: on only while the game keeps up

powerMode.name: Power management mode
powerMode.says: How the graphics card trades power for speed. Maximum performance keeps its clocks up, using more power at idle.

textureQuality.name: Texture filtering quality
textureQuality.says: How carefully textures are filtered. Performance is a little faster and a little blurrier.

anisotropic.name: Anisotropic filtering
anisotropic.says: Sharper textures on surfaces seen at an angle, like floors and roads.

antialiasingMode.name: Antialiasing mode
antialiasingMode.says: Whether the driver leaves smoothing of jagged edges to the game or turns it off.

fxaa.name: Antialiasing - FXAA
fxaa.says: The driver's own quick edge smoothing, on top of the game's. It softens text a little.

shaderCache.name: Shader cache size
shaderCache.says: Room on disk for compiled shaders, so games stutter less the second time. A bigger cache helps games that compile many.

tripleBuffering.name: Triple buffering
tripleBuffering.says: A third frame buffer for smoother frame rates with vertical sync on. Only OpenGL games use it.

threadedOptimization.name: Threaded optimization
threadedOptimization.says: Whether the driver spreads its own work over several CPU cores.

gsync.name: G-SYNC (monitor technology)
gsync.says: Whether the screen's refresh follows the game's frame rate. Fixed refresh turns that off for a game that flickers or stutters with it.

gsyncMode.name: G-SYNC for the whole PC
gsyncMode.says: Whether G-SYNC works in full-screen games only, in windowed games too, or not at all.

refreshRate.name: Preferred refresh rate
refreshRate.says: Whether full-screen games run at the screen's highest refresh rate or the one they ask for.

vrPrerender.name: Virtual reality pre-rendered frames
vrPrerender.says: How many frames a VR game may line up ahead. Fewer cuts lag; more can smooth a struggling game.
